audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly called Spirit Abjuration a 'true-damage passive'. It is a heal, and packet.defects notes the page never named a single Aurora ability.
audit.why: Riot: 'Aurora's spells and attacks exorcise spirits from the enemies she damages. Exorcised spirits follow Aurora around and heal her.' No true damage appears anywhere in her kit. The kit flag on the passive is heal, which is also why the brief asks for Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: whys[6], spikes[3].text, late and wants.foe[1] now describe healing, and the real ability names (Twofold Hex, Across the Veil, The Weirding, Between Worlds) are used throughout.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown-sequencing advice existed anywhere (packet defect) and the cooldowns field had no digits.
audit.why: Across the Veil is 22s at rank 1 and 18s at rank 5; Twofold Hex is 9s with a recast that drags the curse back through you; The Weirding is 15s and hops her backward out of your combo.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten with all three numbers and an explicit wait-for-X line; dosFull[1].d sequences off The Weirding.

audit.why: LeBlanc spikes at 2, 6 and first item; Aurora at 6 with Between Worlds (140/120/100s) and again once healing plus hops outlast a single burst window.
audit.corrected: Kept; phases[6] restated in her terms.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal timing despite the passive being pure sustain.
audit.why: Every spell she lands on you returns a healing spirit, so poke-only patterns lose the attrition.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[N].side read 'Skill' on all seven rows while content win[N] read LeBlanc x6 then Aurora.
audit.why: packet.levelChart agrees with the content layer; the full layer is the outlier and phases[6].why described LeBlanc winning a row the other layer gives to Aurora.
audit.corrected: Sides aligned as one atomic group; phases[6].why rewritten to the Aurora verdict.

edits.before: As Aurora scales into a full build, her sustained poke damage, true-damage passive stacking, and repositioning tools let her outlast and outduel LeBlanc in extended fights, especially since LeBlanc's all-in is a single burst window that can be dodged or survived with enough mobility. If LeBlanc's combo doesn't secure a kill outright, Aurora's kit lets her turn the fight around with sustained damage. This makes the late-game skirmish phase favor Aurora's more resilient scaling kit.
